'''Jeremy Daniel Quastel''' {{post-nominals|country=UK|FRS}}, {{post-nominals|country=CAN|FRSC}} is a Canadian [[mathematician]] specializing in [[probability theory]], [[stochastic processes]] and [[partial differential equations]]. He currently University Professor at the [[University of Toronto Department of Mathematics|University of Toronto]], and previously served as department head from 2017 until 2021.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/jeremy-quastel-35027|accessdate=Sep 17, 2024|title=Fellow Detail Page {{pipe}} Royal Society}}</ref>.

==Career==
Quastel grew up in [[Vancouver]], [[British Columbia]]. He earned his PhD at [[Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences]] at [[New York University]] in 1990; his advisor was [[S. R. Srinivasa Varadhan]]. He was a postdoc at the [[Mathematical Sciences Research Institute]] in Berkeley, then a faculty member at the [[University of California, Davis]] for the next six years.<ref name="crm"/> He returned to Canada in 1998.<ref name="cv"/>

==Research==
Quastel is recognized as one of the top probabilists in the world in the fields of [[Hydrodynamic|hydrodynamic theory]], [[stochastic partial differential equation]]s, and integrable probability.<ref name="crm"/> In particular, his research is on the large scale behaviour of interacting particle systems and stochastic partial differential equations.<ref name="cv"/> Together with Konstantin Matetski and Daniel Remenik, Quastel gave an exact formulation of the [[KPZ fixed point]] in terms of its transition probabilities.<ref name="MQR">{{cite journal |doi=10.4310/acta.2021.v227.n1.a3  |doi-access=free|date=2021 |publisher=International Press of Boston |volume=227|number=1 |pages=115–203 |first1=Konstantin |last1=Matetski |first2=Jeremy |last2=Quastel |first3=Daniel |last3=Remenik |arxiv=1701.00018 |title=The KPZ fixed point |journal=Acta Mathematica}}</ref>

Jeremy Quastel is the grandson of biochemist [[Juda Hirsch Quastel]].
